content.title: Contraindications / Considerations for Heart Transplantation / LVAD
contraindications_and_considerations: Malignancy with poor prognosis (collaboration with oncology to stratify risk of tumour progression/recurrence with immunosuppression)
Irreversible liver dysfunction (cirrhosis) or irreversible renal dysfunction (e.g. creatinine clearance <30 mL/min/1.73 m^2). Combined heart-liver or heart-kidney transplant may be considered
Other serious comorbidity with poor prognosis
Pre-transplant BMI >35 kg/m^2 (weight loss recommended to achieve BMI <35 kg/m^2)
Psychological instability that jeopardizes proper follow-up and intensive therapeutic regimen after heart transplantation
Insufficient social supports to achieve compliant care in the outpatient setting
footnotes_and_notes: Active infection is a relative contraindication to transplant although in some cases of infected LVADs it may actually be an indication.

Elderly age is not an absolute contraindication. Patients aged <65 years might be more appropriate candidates due to overall life expectancy; most programmes accept patients up to 70 years of age. Biological and chronological age must be considered.
Surgical complexity (previous sternotomies, mediastinal radiation, ACHD) should be considered.

Decision pathway to transplantation or LVAD is unique to each patient; eligibility may change over time and can be influenced by factors unrelated to the patient (time on waiting list, centre's surgical experience and resources).
